01 · The brief

One job.

Be the first place a young founder thinks of when they need help to grow.

01FoundersStudents to first-time CEOs, mostly under 30.
02CommunityMentors and founders who've been there.
03ResourcesMentors, credits and grants. One sign-in.

No rockets. No lightbulbs. No handshakes.

02 · Who it's for

Four ages, one door.

A 19-year-old and a 45-year-old mentor should both feel at home.

17–21“Will anyone take me seriously?”
22–25“I'm doing this alone.”
26–30“Just show me the top three.”
30+“Is this worth my name?”
What they shareTo a 19-year-old, premium means being taken seriously.
03 · From words to a mark

Sixty words in. Three left.

We kept only the ones that could carry all three pillars.

The ring Community
circle · belonging · give-back
The door Resources
access · unlock · gateway
The dot Founders
founder · beacon · pin
04 · The idea

Everyone who gets help comes back to give it.

01ArriveOne click and you're in.
02Get helpMentors who've done it, matched to you.
03GrowCredits, grants and programs, when you need them.
04Come backNow you're the mentor someone books.
05 · What a founder gets

The whole campus, in your pocket.

Seven screens from sign-in to the founder circle.

06 · Roots

Born from T-Hub's ring.

T-Hub's ring opens for its name. Ours opens for a founder.

T-Hub
Outpost
07 · The symbol

Three parts. Three pillars.

CommunityThe ringEveryone who's done it before. Left open, so you can walk in.
ResourcesThe doorMentors, credits and grants, behind one sign-in.
FoundersThe dotYou. Arrived, not finished.
Also reads asthe “o” in outposta pin on a mapa beaconan open door
08 · The wordmark

Lowercase, like a first name.

Drawn by hand. No font underneath.

One stroke16 units, round ends.
Soft edgesNothing sharp, like T-Hub's own letters.
One circleo, p and o share the symbol's ring.
OursOriginal, so it can be trademarked.
